content: A replaced OpenAPI schema (with_replacement) needs three touch points; missing any fails downstream tests with E0432 while build.rs stays silent: (1) the schema + property refs in docs/public/api-reference/fabro-api.yaml, (2) the with_replacement entry in lib/foundation/fabro-api/build.rs, (3) the hand-maintained pub use fabro_types::... re-export list inside fabro-api/src/lib.rs's types module (fabro-3488 pass: only (3) made fabro_api::types::ServerSeedsSettings resolve). Corollary: a stale clippy fingerprint can replay an already-fixed E0432 after cargo check passes on the same tree — touch the crate's lib.rs to force a rebuild before re-diagnosing.

description: rustfmt joins backslash-newline continuations INSIDE format! literals into one line but KEEPS the indented whitespace as literal spaces (observed fabro sprint 19: a 21-space run inside a user-facing 422 detail; fmt and clippy cannot see inside literals). User-facing message literals inside format! are written as ONE line or assembled outside format!. Reviewer corollary: verify RENDERED bytes with a tiny print/rustc check, not source literals.
resolution: single-line message literals; render-verify in review

description: Cross-language string editing silently mangles Rust line continuations
resolution: Fixed in the fabro-900e review round: rewrote the two diagnostics in context_append_keys_within_allow.rs with real backslash-newline continuations and exact-equality assertions in the rule test (commit dc5959a80).

description: fabro-tool clippy gate red: nightly clippy denies map_unwrap_or and format_push_string; use map_or_else and write! into the String (std::fmt::Write) instead of push_str(&format!(..)) — seen in create.rs partial-success fix, run 01M1S6VRWQMD56M1X8HWAXDSNN

content: User-facing fabro validate messages must be built as single-line format! strings (multi-line only via backslash-newline continuations verified by compilation), and the rule test must assert the EXACT expected message text, not substring containment. Substring assertions let mangled literals (embedded whitespace runs from scripted edits) pass review and ship garbled CLI output.

name: fabro host-hook transport (petri LocalHooks + worker env)
description: Host hooks run via petri LocalHooks; env_vars() exports FABRO_EVENT/RUN_ID/WORKFLOW/NODE_ID and sh -c .envs() ADDS to the inherited env, so a host hook inherits the WORKER process env - which the server controls via env_clear()+WORKER_ENV_ALLOWLIST (fabro-server/src/spawn_env.rs). cwd is set only when shares_host_filesystem(), false for the Docker provider. Hook script files never enter the workflow-version closure: fabro-manifest workflow_bundler.rs collects DOT references plus config-referenced files in collect_config_files, not run.hooks script paths. Fix path: collect via collect_bundled_file, stage host-side per run, pass a run-scoped env var (fabro-091b).

name: automation-store-error-variant-checklist
description: Adding a variant to AutomationStoreError in lib/components/fabro-automation/src/error.rs requires three coordinated touch points or compilation fails: (1) the variant itself, (2) the exhaustive kind() match at the bottom of error.rs (E0004, surfaces as clippy failure), and (3) the From<AutomationStoreError> for ApiError mapping in lib/apps/fabro-server/src/server/handler/automations.rs (wildcard arm would silently 500 the new variant). Note: scripts/verify.nu swallowed the E0004 clippy stderr on the implementer lane (printed 'FAIL clippy fabro-server' with empty error text); re-running cargo clippy -p <crate> directly reveals the real diagnostic. Applied in fabro-9f4a (run 01M4KZ2BCS4C17PTYRRPANBHJ6): EnvironmentNotFound variant + store.replace validation + 422 with_code mapping + store test.

content: sqlx 0.9 SqlSafeStr gate: sqlx::query/query_with reject dynamically built SQL strings (SqlSafeStr is static-checked). For a small fixed pair-set, prefer ONE fixed-string query per pair over raw_sql or dynamic IN-lists — keeps the injection-audit surface untouched and the bound direction is infallible.

Write plain nested ifs for new code until the whole workspace moves editions.

name: per-request-memo-resolver-kills-n-plus-1
description: When a handler resolves per-row external state (tracker reads) inside a loop, wrap the single resolution in a request-scoped resolver struct holding a HashMap keyed by the natural identity ((project,item)): batched per page/walk, no cross-request invalidation. Pin it with a fake tracker that counts get() calls behind an Arc<AtomicUsize> — assert one call per DISTINCT item per request, not one per record (work#1362, fabro-server orchestration.rs).

name: git-identity-env-outranks-config
description: Git env vars (GIT_COMMITTER_NAME/EMAIL, GIT_AUTHOR_*) outrank BOTH '-c user.*' config AND repo config. When spawning git from tooling processes inside a Fabro run shell (which exports the git bridge identity as GIT_COMMITTER_*/GIT_AUTHOR_*), identity must be pinned via .env() on the Command; git fixtures that assert authorship must pin their identity the same way — a local 'fn run' in the tests module shadows the glob-imported helper and pins every fixture git call in one spot.

name: cross-vendor-fork-feature-gate
description: When a vendored fork crate (vendor/petri) must call a trait method that only exists in ANOTHER vendored fork (vendor/sandbox-driver's OneShot::evict_lru_images), the method cannot be referenced unconditionally: the petri workspace resolves sandbox-driver from upstream lithoscomputer main, where the method does not exist, so its own --locked build breaks. Pattern: gate the call behind a cargo feature on the vendored crate (env-image-evict, default off, documented in its Cargo.toml), and switch it on from the CONSUMING fabro workspace via a feature-carrying workspace dependency entry (root Cargo.toml petri_executor_sandbox + a comment-only dep in fabro-petri). Fabro builds get the fork behavior; the vendor workspace keeps building against upstream; fork-only presence tests pin the gated pieces in every build (work#1440).

content: sessions.rs (fabro-server handler) carries FOUR surfaces in one 2.5k-line file: model selection/canonicalization, the ask tool policy, the turn runtime, SSE persistence. ADR-0046's supervisor capability cuts across all four — land a split FIRST (session_models module; ask-policy module owning the allowlist+prompt with the capability mode as parameter) or the capability switch threads a patchwork. Timing bet: pays only if ADR-0046 lands soon (items #1451-53) — it will.

fabro-tool's RunSummaryResult is a hand-flattened string-typed parallel of fabro_types::Run and has ALREADY drifted (no claimed_seed_id, usage, timing, ask_fabro, diff/pull_request). The compact shape is legitimate (model token budget) — the hand-sync is the smell. Fix shape when a missing field first misleads an agent: a from_run constructor colocated with Run in fabro-types + a parity pin (precedent: fabro-tool/create.rs parity tests).

The scheduler tick composition is hand-mirrored by its test harness: run_due_schedules_once re-implements the breaker prefix by hand and SKIPS the provider gate, fact writes, held filter and lag watchdog - while the last three incident classes (work#603 unpause ordering, work#1234 discarded refusal body, work#1162 hold classification) lived in exactly the skipped composition. Fix shape when touched next: extract one scheduler_tick(state, planner, lag_watchdog, now) -> TickOutcome containing the ordered pass; the production loop reduces to select-shutdown + tick; the test calls the same tick. The pure cores (planner, lag watchdog, refusal detail) are already well-tested.

title: Architect reads both sides; loop-to-core promotion is first-class
rationale: Operator directive 2026-11-18. The former lib/apps observable-only binding (months old) pointed both reviewer generations away from the foundation's deepest candidates; the Rust foundation pass found five Strong items there in one walk (#1457-#1461). The scope is deliberately BIDIRECTIONAL: loop-to-core promotion candidates are first-class - script logic that has become general-purpose moves into the core as platform work items (first example: the quiet-cause verdict #1459, moving stall-check/CLI re-derivations into a server read model). Vendor stays engine-frozen (ADR-0027, observations only).

name: fork-feature-pure-decision-seam
description: When a vendored-fork feature must keep the crate compilable against upstream (feature off), split the behavior into a pure ungated decision function over plain values (cook_path over Result<bool, DriverError> in petri executor-sandbox image_build.rs, work#1463) plus a thin cfg(feature)-gated wrapper calling the fork-only trait method (OneShot::image_present). The pure seam runs in the vendored workspace suite against upstream deps, so fork pins stay executable everywhere.

name: slack-service-home
description: Arch-review candidate (2026-11-19, Worth exploring): SlackService (~550 lines) lives inside fabro-server/src/server.rs (4,786 lines total) while the crate named fabro-slack stays a thin API wrapper — the lifecycle domain (breaker messages, ask-question thread registry, connection runtime, error sanitization) has no home in its own crate. Deepening when this surface next gets touched: move the service behind a narrow interface into its own module or fabro-slack; server.rs keeps AppState + router assembly. Deletion-test positive; no ADR contradicted (ADR-0039 stage D decided the answer channel, not the module seat).

name: cli-connection-ladders
description: Arch-review candidate (2026-11-19, Worth exploring): fabro-cli/src/server_client.rs (850 lines) re-derives the resolve-credential → probe/connect → named-recovery (auto-start, the work#1174 channel-orphaned bail) → re-resolve → transport ladder in FOUR connect_* entry points; the incident diagnostics sit inline in one ladder branch. Deepening: one connection builder whose steps are the shared ladder, the four public functions reduced to policy choices; each recovery unit-testable without spawning a server. File is otherwise cohesive — the win is diagnostics locality.

name: work-store-split
description: Arch-review candidate (2026-11-19, Speculative — revisit when the grant window next needs structural work): fabro-work/src/store.rs (2,209 lines, one WorkStore impl) holds two bounded contexts — the hot conflict-prone claim ledger (ADR-0032, served by hold.rs) and the cold observation-link/decision store (ADR-0038/0044). Split risk: a move, not a concentration. The fabro-store precedent (seven focused stores over one SQLite) is the target shape.
